howItWorks.title: How MARCALL works
howItWorks.subtitle: A receptionist that never sleeps, in five steps. No code, no complicated screens — just conversation.
howItWorks.s1Body: The call comes into MARCALL’s number — or is forwarded from your existing number when you don’t pick up. Nothing to change in your PBX: just enable no-answer forwarding.
howItWorks.s2Body: In under a second. Greets with your business name, in Mexican Spanish or English depending on the caller. If they switch languages mid-sentence, MARCALL switches with them.
howItWorks.s3Body: Books the appointment in your Google Calendar against real availability, takes a complete message, answers FAQs from the script you wrote, qualifies the lead, or transfers to your team if needed.
howItWorks.s4Body: A WhatsApp message hits the owner’s phone and an email lands with the reason, outcome, and full transcript. The appointment shows up directly in Google Calendar. Everything is logged in your dashboard for audit.
howItWorks.s5Body: You review transcripts, edit the script wherever something feels off, adjust services or answers — and MARCALL learns. It’s not a black box: it’s your receptionist with her notebook visible.
howItWorks.endCtaBody: No card. Set up in 5 minutes. Cancel anytime.

items.q: Do I need a credit card to try it?
items.a: No. You start with 7 days totally free, no card. We only ask for the card if you decide to continue on day 8.
Mexican Spanish and English, with automatic mid-call code-switching. MARCALL detects the caller’s language in the first words and adapts.

items.q: Can I use my current phone number?
items.a: Yes. You configure call forwarding for unanswered calls (or all calls, if you prefer) to your MARCALL number. Works with Telmex, AT&T, Megacable, and any VoIP carrier. Takes under 5 minutes. If you don’t want to touch your number, we provide a temporary MARCALL number.
5 minutes to configure the assistant (hours, services, FAQs). If you request a fresh MARCALL number, the carrier KYC (Twilio) takes 3–10 business days depending on the number type.

items.q: Is recording calls legal in Mexico?
items.a: Yes, with notice at the start. MARCALL automatically plays the disclosure phrase at the beginning of each call — we comply with LFPDPPP and IFT guidelines.
Yes. AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, audit log of every administrative access, and ARCO rights available from the customer dashboard. More details on our security page.

items.q: Does it work with my calendar?
items.a: Google Calendar yes — OAuth connection in 30 seconds. Outlook and Apple Calendar are on the roadmap for Q1 2026.

items.q: How many concurrent calls can it handle?
items.a: Unlimited on the Crece, Multi-sucursal, and Empresa/Agencia plans. Inicia is limited to 2 concurrent (sufficient for most SMBs).

items.q: How does it differ from global competitors?
items.a: Honestly: MARCALL is optimized for Mexican Spanish (regional accents, idioms, Mexican formality) and pricing in MXN with no FX surprises. Global competitors (Air.ai, Synthflow, Bland) are tuned for English and bill in USD. If your customer base is 100% Mexico, MARCALL fits you better.

vsHumano.title: MARCALL vs. human receptionist
vsHumano.subtitle: The honest comparison. MARCALL doesn’t replace your team — it picks up what they can’t reach.
vsHumano.caveatBody: MARCALL doesn’t replace the human touch of a specialized team — it complements it. For complex queries, high-value sales, or delicate complaints, MARCALL transfers the call to your team in seconds. The point is to free your people from 80% of routine calls so they can focus on the 20% that actually moves the business.

security.heroLead: MARCALL handles voice calls, transcripts, and personal data on behalf of Mexican businesses. We take that responsibility seriously: encryption in transit and at rest, multi-tenant isolation, audit logging, and a compliance program aligned with LFPDPPP, GDPR, and SOC 2. To report a vulnerability, email security@careofaddress.com — acknowledged within 72 hours.
security.section1Sub: What’s already in place and what’s on the roadmap.
inPlaceItems: Encryption in transit (TLS 1.3) on every public endpoint
Encryption at rest (AES-256) on the production database (Supabase)
Password hashing with bcrypt (cost 12), never plaintext
Multi-tenant isolation enforced on every API route, RLS-ready architecture
Append-only audit log for authentication, admin actions, and webhooks
Per-IP rate limiting on auth, voice tools, and the general API
Webhook signature verification for Stripe, Vapi, and Twilio
PII redaction in application logs (password, token, INE, RFC, CURP)
Automated dependency scanning (npm audit) on every deploy
Principle of least privilege for all subprocessors
comingItems: HIPAA Safe-Harbor configuration for Empresa Salud tier — Q3 2026
Annual third-party penetration test (first one Q3 2026)

section2Items.v: Privacy notice published, in-product ARCO process with 20 business-day SLA, INAI registration.
DPA available for European customers; SCCs in place with every subprocessor.
Fully handled by Stripe — MARCALL never sees card data. SAQ-A applicable.
Telemarketing/voice conduct rules baked into TOS and every assistant’s system prompt.
Available on the Empresa Salud tier. BAA on request.
Bilingual notice inserted at call start by every assistant.

security.arcoCancel: Cancellation — remove data once it is no longer required.

security.section6Lead: If you found a security issue, email security@careofaddress.com. Acknowledged within 72 hours. Good-faith research is welcome and will not be subject to legal action as long as third-party data and production services are respected.
